2014 QCCS 6642

Droit de la famille — 143455

JL 4486

SUPERIOR COURT

(Family Division)

CANADA

PROVINCE
OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

N° :

500-12-305589-107

DATE :

DECEMBER 12, 2014

______________________________________________________________________

PRESIDING :

THE HONOURABLE

PIERRE
LABELLE, J.S.C.

______________________________________________________________________

H. E.

Plaintiff

-vs-

D. A.

Defendant

JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

I.   INTRODUCTION

[
1
]

The Court is seized with an amended motion filed
by Plaintiff to modify accessory measures and safeguard order and an amended
motion filed by Defendant to modify the schedule of shared custody of the
children of the parties and other measures.

[
2
]

An amended agreement as to accessory measures
was ratified in the divorce judgment pronounced on December 13, 2011.

[
3
]

The parties consider that since the signature of
the amended agreement, there has been a change of circumstances in their lives.

[
4
]

The mother is requesting the following:

a)   Child support payable by the father
to the mother for the benefit of the two minor children in the amount of
$642.72 per month retroactively to 2012;

b)   Spousal support of $2,000 per month;

c)   New custodial arrangements;

d)   That the child X be removed from
the regular school system and be homeschooled by her as well as in a community
centre;

e)   Specific orders to the father concerning
children’s schools and activities;

f)   No obligation to have to
participate in a mediation session in case of disagreements.

[
5
]

The father is requesting the following:

a)   Determine the child support payable by him;

b)   New custodial arrangements;

c)   Order the mother to let the children attend the
regular school system;

d)   Order the mother to cease her defamation
campaign against him.

[
6
]

The parties filed a partial agreement dated
October 23, 2014 by which they settled the claim with regards to the child support
arrears owed by the father to the mother for the period of January, 2012 to
October 31, 2014.

[
7
]

Consequently, the Court shall decide on child
support beginning November 1
st
, 2014.

II.   THE FACTUAL CONTEXT

[
8
]

The parties were married on March 14, 2002 in Town A. The mother is of Jewish faith and the father of Catholic faith.

[
9
]

On December 13, 2011, a judgment of divorce was pronounced.

[
10
]

The mother is presently working on call for the [Center
A] as a ″Aide
natale / agente administrative″. In 2013, she has earned a gross annual salary of $9,622.57.

[
11
]

The father is a college teacher under contract
since 2009. In 2013, he has earned $96,825.25. He testifies that he has
accepted other contracts in order to attain this total income. He considers
that he works hard to meet his liabilities. Probably, for many reasons, his
income will be reduced next year.

[
12
]

The parties have two children, Y, born on [...],
2002, presently 12 years old, and X, born on [...], 2005, presently 9 years
old.

[
13
]

Y is attending high school while X is attending
elementary school. However, X was recently diagnosed with Attention Deficit
Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). X is in a regular classroom with some resources
support. A psychologist report
[1]
states that X would benefit from a medication on a trial basis.

[
14
]

The mother has been giving medication to X
without the father’s consent. This medication was recommended by a psychiatrist
and prescribed by the family doctor. She testifies that she had received the father’s
approval as long as he could get a second opinion beforehand from another
doctor as to what might be the side effects of the medication.

[
15
]

While taking the medication, X became more
aggressive towards his mother.
[2]
Following an incident at school, the family doctor advised the mother
to stop the medication.

[
16
]

The mother explains that since September 2014,
she has been spending almost every lunch time one-on-one at home with X in
order to calm him for the rest of the afternoon.

[
17
]

In addition, she spends many hours each day to
help X with his homework. Considering his global development delay, the mother
has searched for different schools offering classes with smaller groups. The
result reveals that these schools have a long waiting list of at least one
year.

[
18
]

The mother suggests that she could homeschooled X
in the morning and that he could attend an external homeschooling environment
in the afternoon and evening, therefore allowing him to socialize with other
children.

[
19
]

If this happens, the mother would not be able to
work on a fulltime basis and consequently, she is requesting spousal support
from the father.

[
20
]

The parties consider that new accessory measures
should be introduced as both testified on the difficulties they encounter
regarding the access rights and the drop off and pick up times of the children
in relation with the shared custody and the holiday and vacation schedules.

[
21
]

Finally, the mother maintains having been raped
by the father in March 2008. In October 2008, she filed an application
[3]
in virtue of the
Crime Victims Compensation Act (IVAC)
. The
name of the person allegedly responsible for the crime is not disclosed in that
application.

[
22
]

She testifies that the name of the father was
disclosed later. She admits to having talked about the assault to a few closed
friends, at least four persons.

[
23
]

On May 30, 2012, she reported the assault at a
police station. Sergeant Annie Prévost of the Montreal Police Department
testifies that after investigation, no criminal charges were filed against the
father.

[
24
]

The father denies vigorously having committed an
assault towards the mother. These allegations affect his personal and
professional life and, as a result, he feels that the allegations constitute a “sword
of Damocles” over his head and his career. As a result, the father claims that
he was forced to resign as a member of a PhD committee and asks the Court that
this defamation campaign be stopped.

III   ANALYSIS AND DISCUSSION

3.1
Change of circumstances

[
25
]

Both parties admit that a material change of
circumstances has occurred since the signature of the amended agreement as to
accessory measures and consent to judgment on June 16, 2011. The Court is
satisfied that there has been a significant change in the situation that
existed in December 2011.

[
26
]

The mother is no longer receiving indemnities from
IVAC and works on call as a ″aide natale / agente administrative″. The father is approaching permanent status as a college teacher
and has access to a flexible teaching schedule giving him a larger availability
during the week to spend time with the children. In July 2014, X was diagnosed with
ADHD profile and suffers from a global development delay and of dyspraxia. Y is
12 years old and she is attending high school.

[
27
]

Finally, the parties are asking the Court to
determine if X should continue to attend the regular school system and to
determine new and clear custodial arrangements.

3.2
Education of X

[
28
]

Notwithstanding the attribution of custody to a
parent, both parties continue to exercise jointly parental authority and to
retain the right to supervise the education of the children.

[
29
]

If the parties are unable to agree, the Court
must intervene as provided at section 604 Q.C.C.:

Art. 604.
In the case of difficulties relating to the
exercise of parental authority, the person having parental authority may refer
the matter to the court, which will decide in the interest of the child after
fostering the conciliation of the parties.

[
30
]

Unfortunately in this case, the parties are
unable to agree as to the educational plan X should follow. To decide, the
Court shall keep in mind the interest of the child.

[
31
]

X is currently attending third grade at a
regular elementary school. He needs some resource support with a modified
mathematic program and an adapted French program.

[
32
]

X has difficulties to control his emotions. Some
incidents occurred which resulted in a few days of suspension. The mother
decided to keep him at home for lunch in order to help him stay calm at school
for the afternoon.

[
33
]

The mother spends almost three hours a day for
homework. She maintains that X needs her presence to keep his interest in
school.

[
34
]

According to verbal recommendations by a
psychiatrist and a psychologist, the mother asserts that X should attend a
school with smaller classes. Though, she mentions that there is a long waiting
list, at least a year, to obtain a place in this kind of school.

[
35
]

In the face of the difficulty, the mother
considers that homeschooling is a viable option. She undertakes to comply with
all requirements of the Ministère de l’Éducation, du Loisir et du Sport (MELS).

[
36
]

At the other hand, the father wants X to stay at
the actual school since he is used to it and also, because his friends are
attending the same school. His Individual Education Plan 2014-2015 is positive
[4]
and his Interim Report Card 2014-2015, cycle two, is mostly
satisfactory
[5]
.

[
37
]

The father agrees for X to try some medication
and to observe the effect on him. He thinks that X has a motivation problem due
to his mother telling him that he will be homeschooled. The father underlines
that he knows how to motivate his son and, furthermore, that his son would
benefit from his teaching experience.

[
38
]

X underwent a psychological assessment done by
Dr. Karen Hardoon, psychologist, on October 14, 2014 which was filed by the mother.

[
39
]

Dr. Hardoon’s assessment and her testimony
demonstrate that:

•           A diagnosis of a mild intellectual impairment is not
made for the moment;

•           Learning is difficult for him considering
his deficits for comprehension, working memory and processing speed, as well as
his severe ADHD;

•           X has impairments in his conceptual,
practical and social functioning;

•           X’s needs would best be met in a small,
structured and specialized classroom setting (10 to 15 students);

•           A one to one educational relationship is
not appropriate;

•           X would benefit from a medication trial;

•           If X is less impulsive and controls his
emotions, more will be his attention.

[
40
]

The Court will not opine as to the mother’s
demand to provide homeschooling to X. The interest of the child would not be well
served.

[
41
]

There is no expert’s recommendation to
homeschooling X. Homeschooling could be an enriching experience for the child
but the recommendation contemplates a small teacher to pupil ratio for a more
individualized attention and guided instruction.

[
42
]

The Court is of the view that homeschooling is
not a valid alternative for X to obviate a waiting list. Homeschooling by the mother
could compromise the best interest of the child.

[
43
]

There is no necessity to remove X from his
school environment considering that he could benefit from a medication trial
and that his father confirms his involvement towards his son.

[
44
]

The Court determines that on the balance of
probabilities, the evidence does not prove that the interest of the child is to
be homeschooled.

3.3
The mother’s alimentary pension

[
45
]

Based on the above decision dismissing the mother’s
request for homeschooling X, the Court will not allow a spousal support for her
planned contribution.

[
46
]

But the mother is of the view that it was
difficult for her to return to work on a fulltime basis. She has explained that
she spends many hours with X to be one-on-one with him for lunch time and
school works. To meet his needs, she is prevented from working fulltime.

[
47
]

The grounds to claim a spousal support are based
on a unilateral and personal choice and, using her own words ″to calm X for the rest of the
afternoon″.

[
48
]

She received a lump sum from IVAC in June 2012
because she was able to work. In 2013, she worked on a 6-8 weeks contract in
administration at the Lakeshore Hospital. After that, she said that she was not
available during the week, but only during the weekend.

[
49
]

The effort given by the Mother is noticeable but
no more than any other parent in the same circumstances and considering her young
age, there is no reason not to look for a fulltime work. Efforts on her part are
needed to be part of the workforce.

[
50
]

Consequently, the spousal support will not be
granted.

3.4
Joint custody

[
51
]

The father seeks joint custody for his two
children.

[
52
]

The general principle with matters dealing with
the custody is the interest of the child and the respect of his rights
[6]
.

[
53
]

As to the issue of joint custody, many criteria
must be considered
[7]
, especially:

•           The interest of the child;

•           The parental abilities;

•           The communication between the parents;

•           The relationship of the child with each parent;

•           The physical distance between the residences of the
parents.

[
54
]

Regardless of the form of custody, both parents
continue to exercise parental authority together
[8]
and
the child continues to benefit from the input of each parent.

[
55
]

Consequently, both parents retain the right to
supervise the maintenance and education of the child
[9]
.

[
56
]

In the Court’s opinion, joint custody should be
seriously considered when many of the above-mentioned criteria are met.

[
57
]

The children are 12 and 9 years old. Their
interest commands to maintain a close relationship with both parents which will
contribute to their blossoming.

[
58
]

There is no doubt that presently, the mother
represents the prevailing parental figure in the children’s life being the
custodial parent. However, this status does not entitle her to make decisions
alone and impose such decisions on the other parent.

[
59
]

For example, when the mother, on school days,
decided to keep X at home for lunchtime in spite of the father’s objection.

[
60
]

As well, when the mother told X that he would be
homeschooled without any father’s approbation
[10]
.

[
61
]

Similarly, when the mother gave X the prescribed
medication even though the father had asked her to wait in order for him to
obtain more information about side effects.

[
62
]

The Court is dealing with two parties who are
good parents but are unable to cooperate in the exercise of their parental
authority, despite their excellent parental capacities.

[
63
]

The Court finds that communications between the
parents are workable. They are able to communicate with respect to their
relationship with the children in a calm and respectful manner. The Court holds
that the father is a fully capable and empathic parent.

[
64
]

The evidence supports that there is a great deal
of love and affection and significant emotional ties between Y and X and their
parents. They are patient and caring. They both want the best for their
children.

[
65
]

The children’s parents live in suitable
residential accommodations. The distance between the two houses, though not
ideal, does not appear to be an obstacle. The children are at walking distance
from the mother’s residence and the school. From the father’s residence, the
children must commute by train. Door to door, they spend between 25 and 40
minutes. The distance does not appear to be an issue for them.

[
66
]

The Court is of the view that all the necessary
demonstrations have been made to show that shared custody is feasible in the
present matter and will better serve the best interest of the children than the
current arrangement, where the mother has sole custody.

[
67
]

Their stability is not compromised. The shared
custody will enhance their emotional ties with the father as well as with the mother.

3.5
Child support

[
68
]

As of November 1
st
, 2014, alimentary
support will be calculated on the shared custody basis. Support is based on
incomes of $92,454.02 (father) and $9,622.57 (mother) respectively appearing on
the Schedule 1 filed jointly.

3.6
Campaign of defamation

[
69
]

Defendant states in his proceedings that:

The Plaintiff persists in spreading
her false and calumnious allegations regarding the Defendant thus exacting a
psychological toll on the Defendant and affecting his personal and professional
life
[11]
.

[
70
]

Defendant seeks for an order to cease
immediately her defamation campaign against him.

[
71
]

The Court is of the view that this order is
tantamount to an interlocutory injunction. The Court will not grant this order
for two reasons.

[
72
]

Firstly, the general terms of the order do not
respect article 751 C.C.P which requires describing a particular act of
operation. The order is vague and imprecise and not susceptible of execution.

[
73
]

Secondly, article 752 C.C.P. requires that the applicant appears to be entitled to an apparent right. This is not such
a case. In considering this issue, the Court shall decide on the merits only
after a complete hearing to determine the invoked Defendant’s rights.
Consequently, the Court will reserve his recourse.

FOR THESE
REASONS, THE COURT:

[
74
]

RATIFIES
the
partial agreement judgment on accessory measures signed by the parties on
October 23, 2014, reading as follows:

[
75
]

ORDERS
the
parties to conform to it;

[
76
]

DECLARES
that
there has been a change of circumstances since the divorce judgment and
consent;

[
77
]

MODIFIES
the
amended agreement as to accessory measures and consent to judgment signed by
the parties on June 16, 2011 and ratified by the judgment of divorce rendered
between the parties on December 13, 2011;

[
78
]

REPLACES
the
provisions numbered 20, 21, 22, 23 and 31 of said amended agreement;

[
79
]

GRANTS
shared custody
to the parents, on an alternate weekly basis, starting each week on Friday
after school or summer day camp or at 4:30 p.m. at the other parent’s house, or
at 4:30 p.m. at a mutually agreed upon location;

[
80
]

GRANTS
access
rights on Wednesday after school until Thursday morning at school every other
week to the parent who does not exercise custody that week, during school year;

[
81
]

SUGGESTS
that the
parties keep a regular journal concerning the children to be exchanged between
them. The parents will note therein the children’s medical, school, and other
appointment details concerning any illness, medication and particular problems
requiring weekly follow-ups.

[
82
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the father on Father’s Day from 9:00 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. and to the mother
on Mother’s Day from 9:00 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.;

[
83
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the father for the week of Christmas, including Christmas Day, each
year, and access rights for the following week to the mother;

[
84
]

GRANTS
access
rights alternatively on New Year’s Eve to New Year’s Day at noon. This year,
the children will be with the mother.

[
85
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the father for Easter each year, including Good Friday and Easter
Monday, starting on Thursday after school and ending on Tuesday morning at
school.

[
86
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the father for Thanksgivings each year, starting on Friday after
school and ending on Tuesday morning at school;

[
87
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the mother for the first and second night of Rosh Hashanah and
Passover each year;

[
88
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the mother for Yom Kippur from sundown to sundown the next day;

[
89
]

GRANTS
access
rights to the mother for the first two nights of Chanukah;

[
90
]

ORDERS
that, in
the event the Jewish and Christian Holidays overlap in the same time period,
the mother will have custody on all odd years and the father on all even years;

[
91
]

GRANTS
the mother,
for the week of school spring break, custody on all even years and the father
on all odd years;

[
92
]

GRANTS
each
parent two consecutive weeks with the children during the summer vacations,
ordering them to exchange the dates by May 15
th
of each year. The mother
shall have priority on all odd years and the father on all even years;

[
93
]

GRANTS
the father
permission to travel to Cuba during school spring break as well as vacation
time;

[
94
]

ORDERS
the mother
to sign and remit all necessary documents to the father in order for him and
the children to pursue their trip;

[
95
]

ORDERS
the parent
travelling with the children to provide the other parent with an address and
telephone number where the children will be staying, where they may be reached
during vacation time and the specific days that they will be away;

[
96
]

GRANTS
each
parent an evening telephone access right to the children every 48 hours as well
as on special occasions such as birthdays or special activities or other circumstances,
at a reasonable time for a reasonable duration;

[
97
]

ORDERS
the
parents to let Y use her cellular phone to communicate freely with them;

[
98
]

ORDERS
the
parents to let the children pursue their studies in their respective school in
accordance with the school schedule;

[
99
]

ORDERS
each party
to agree to share all significant information with regards to the children including,
without limitation, their education, health and extracurricular activities;

[
100
]

ORDERS
for each
parent to promptly inform the other if an unanticipated event access to the
children, including, without limiting the generality of the preceding, school
absence, medical problems;

[
101
]

ORDERS
the
parents to agree that, should the custodial parent be unavailable to care for
the children for a period of more than twenty-four (24) hours, the other parent
shall be offered the opportunity to be with the minor children prior to calling
upon any other third party;

[
102
]

ORDERS
both
parents not to denigrate the other parent in front of the children;

[
103
]

ORDERS
the
parties not to discuss any differences, including this litigation, in front of
the children;

[
104
]

ORDERS
the
parties not to criticize the conduct and behaviour of the other parent in front
of the children;

[
105
]

ORDERS
the father
to pay to the mother for the two children of the parties, Y and X, child
support in accordance with the child support guidelines in the amount of
$583.75 a month as of November 1, 2014;

[
106
]

RESERVES
the
father’s right with respect to the issue of defamation;

[
107
]

ORDERS

provisional execution of the present judgment notwithstanding appeal;

[
108
]

WITHOUT COSTS
.
